views.name: race_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time
FROM races

params.when_to_use: List or inspect races as entities (one row per race_id) with their scheduling and session timestamps — e.g., show all races in a year, or show race metadata including circuit_id, name, date/time, and session datetimes. | Join races to dimensions or facts at the race grain (race_id) to bring in race-level attributes before further joins/aggregations — e.g., attach race metadata to results_fact or pit_stops_measure by race_id. | Filter or paginate races by race attributes (year, round, circuit_id) — e.g., build calendar views, timetables, or race-detail pages where each row represents a single race.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need competitor-level rows (drivers, constructors) per race: this view has one row per race_id, so reusing it for driver- or constructor-level questions will silently drop multiplicity and undercount — use a join to driver/constructor facts instead. | Do not use for aggregations that require session-level or lap-level granularity (e.g., count of pit stops, average lap time per race) because this view contains only race-level metadata and no repeated rows for sessions or laps; aggregating over this view will produce counts of races, not counts of events within races. | Do not use when you need validated timing results (fastest laps, qualifying positions, finishing positions): timing and rank-related details are not present here, so reusing this view will omit critical columns and produce incorrect results if the query assumes those columns exist. | Do not use when you need cohort-restricted race sets derived from results (e.g., races where a particular driver participated or finished): this view does not encode participation/cohort membership and will not filter properly without joining a participation/result table. | Do not use when you need session-level ordering or multiple session occurrences per race (e.g., multiple FP sessions beyond the fixed fp1/fp2/fp3 columns): the view flattens sessions into fixed columns and cannot represent multiple rows per session, so reusing it for variable-session analyses will be wrong.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need per-driver per-race outcomes — it has driver/constructor identifiers and finishing positions, whereas race_basic only contains race metadata and would miss multiplicity and result fields. | use qualifying_grid instead when you need qualifying position grids or per-driver qualifying rows — qualifying_grid is a JOIN that produces one row per driver per race for qualifying, while race_basic is one row per race and cannot represent individual qualifying records. | use pit_stops_measure or race_pitstop_summary instead when you need pit-stop counts or summaries by race — those are measures/aggregates over pit stop events, whereas race_basic only provides race-level metadata and would undercount or misrepresent event-level totals. | use lap_times_measure or driver_lap_aggregates when you need lap-level or driver-lap aggregates — they provide repeated rows per lap or aggregated metrics per driver/race; race_basic would incorrectly be used as the event source and lose lap multiplicity. | use driver_dim or constructor_dim when you need driver or constructor attributes — those sibling dimension tables contain entity attributes for drivers/constructors, while race_basic contains only race attributes and cannot substitute for person/team dimensions.

views.description: Normalized projection of races with canonical key and descriptive attributes. Use this as a stable race dimension when joining facts — preserves race identifiers and common attributes (year, round, circuit_id, name, date, time). | Use for: List races by year/round/circuit; Join races to results/qualifying/pit stops; Filter races by date or by having sprint/quali

views.name: driver_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers

params.when_to_use: Lookups or joins that need one row per driver identified by driver_id (e.g., enriching event-level or season-level facts with driver attributes). | Displaying driver attributes (driver_ref, number, code, forename, surname, dob, nationality, url) for a specific driver or list of drivers without changing aggregation (detail-level attribute retrieval). | Presenting driver profile pages or reports that show static demographic/identity fields for drivers (no time/season/race context implied). | Joining to facts where the fact row is already at the driver_id grain so joins do not introduce duplication (e.g., driver-level aggregates that were aggregated to driver_id).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not reuse this view to answer questions that require a different grain such as driver-by-season, driver-by-race, or driver-by-lap — this view has one row per driver (driver_id) and lacks any season/race/lap context, so joining it to a fact at a more granular grain can silently duplicate rows or under/over-count if not properly aggregated first. | Avoid reusing it to filter or limit to a cohort defined by race/season/round/team/constructor or time window — the view contains no season, race, constructor or date-scoped membership information, so cohort filters applied only to this view would be meaningless and could return drivers who were never in that cohort. | Do not use this view when you need historical or time-variant driver attributes (e.g., number/code changes across seasons) — it exposes only the current/stored attribute values from drivers table and will silently misattribute historical rows. | Not appropriate for computing measures/aggregates (counts, sums, averages) that expect aggregated driver-level metrics across contexts — it provides attributes only; using it in place of an aggregated view may produce incorrect counts if the join multipliers are not managed. | Do not substitute this view for any view that encodes joined or derived driver metrics (season points, ranks, lap aggregates, fastest laps, pitstop summaries). Those views contain aggregated or joined logic that this simple dimension does not provide and replacing them will drop essential computations.
params.comparison: use driver_season_points instead when you need driver-level points broken down by season — driver_dim has the same driver identity but driver_season_points provides season-scoped aggregated points and should be used for season-level analyses. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor when you need race-level results or to compute race-by-driver measures — those sibling views include per-race/per-result rows and metrics; driver_dim only provides identity attributes and would lead to incorrect cardinality if used in their place. | use qualifying_grid or fastest_lap_per_race when you need per-race/per-session performance metrics (grid positions or fastest lap info) — driver_dim lacks session/race performance data and will not answer those questions. | use driver_lap_aggregates or lap_times_measure when you need lap-level or aggregated lap metrics by driver — those contain lap-level or aggregated measures; driver_dim is purely an attribute dimension and cannot substitute them. | use constructor_dim when you need constructor/team identity attributes — constructor_dim has similar semantics for constructors (one row per constructor) while driver_dim is keyed by driver_id and cannot provide constructor attributes. | use constructor_season_points or constructor_season_rank when working with season-scoped constructor aggregates/ranks — driver_dim differs because it is driver-scoped and non-aggregated.

views.description: Normalized driver dimension projection exposing identity columns suitable for joins and reporting (keeps forename/surname/code/number and dob). Use whenever driver descriptive attributes are needed. | Use for: Lookup driver details by id or name; Join driver attributes to lap_times, results, pit_stops

views.name: constructor_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructor_id,
  constructor_ref,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors

params.when_to_use: Look up constructor-level attributes (static properties) for a given constructor_id — e.g., 'what is the name/nationality/url for constructor_id = X'. | Join-leveling when you need one row per constructor (the natural grain is constructor_id) to attach constructor reference data to other datasets without changing their row counts. | Building catalogs or dropdowns of constructors where each constructor appears once.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to answer questions that require per-race, per-season, per-driver, or per-result aggregation — this view has one row per constructor_id only, so joining it expecting multiple rows (e.g., 'races per constructor', 'wins per constructor in 2020') will undercount or produce incorrect cardinality. | Avoid using it to filter by cohorts that are not present in constructors (for example recent-season membership). The view contains no season or race columns, so filtering by season/race after joining to this view will not restrict constructors to those active in that season unless you also join to a fact that contains season/race. | Do not use it as a source of measures (counts, sums, averages). This view exposes only descriptive identifiers and strings (constructor_id, constructor_ref, name, nationality, url) and contains no aggregated metrics — using it where numeric measures are expected will silently return NULL or zero when aggregated incorrectly. | Don't reuse it as a replacement for views that encode joins/filters (JOIN/AGG/RANK). For example, it will not provide grid/qualifying/order/season-points information; substituting it for those will lose the essential join keys and result rows.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need per-result/per-race/per-season measures — results_fact has the event-level and performance metrics that constructor_dim lacks. | use constructor_season_points instead when you need aggregated points per constructor per season — constructor_season_points has season grain and aggregated points; constructor_dim is static, single-row-per-constructor. | use constructor_season_rank instead when you need ranking information across seasons — constructor_season_rank provides ranked/aggregated outputs by season that constructor_dim does not. | use results_with_driver_constructor when you need combined driver+constructor entries for each result row — results_with_driver_constructor preserves result-level grain and will produce multiple rows per constructor as appropriate, whereas constructor_dim will not. | use race_basic when you need race-level context (season, round, date) in combination with constructor info — race_basic contains race identifiers and metadata missing from constructor_dim. | use qualifying_grid or fastest_lap_per_race when you need event-specific performance (qualifying positions or fastest lap per race) — those sibling views include event-level performance and joins that constructor_dim does not provide.

views.description: Constructor/team dimension projection preserving identifiers and descriptive attributes for joins and reporting. | Use for: Join constructor info to results/constructor_standings/constructor_results; List constructors and their nationality

views.name: lap_times_measure
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  lap,
  position,
  time,
  milliseconds
FROM lap_times

params.when_to_use: Ask for the raw lap-by-lap timing records for each race and driver (one row per race_id, driver_id, lap) — e.g., "what was driver X's time on lap N in race Y?" | Joinable source of lap-level fields (position, time, milliseconds) when you need to compute custom aggregates or windows yourself (e.g., compute average lap time per stint or detect lap time trends), because the view exposes the atomic lap rows without additional aggregation. | Reconstruct sequences of laps (ordered by lap) per driver/race for event-level analyses that require exact lap sequence and per-lap timestamps or offsets.
params.when_not_to_use: Use this view when you want aggregated metrics per driver, race, or season (e.g., total race time, average across all laps, best lap per race) — WHY: lap_times is at the lap grain (race_id, driver_id, lap) so aggregating here requires explicit GROUP BY; using it as if it already represented aggregates risks double-counting or incorrect aggregation. | Use this view as a record of participants or final finishing order — WHY: it contains per-lap 'position' which can change each lap; treating 'position' here as final result yields incorrect cohorts and silently-wrong answers if you expect finishing position (use results_fact instead). | Use this view as the canonical source of pit stop events or stint boundaries — WHY: pit stops are event-level, not necessarily aligned to lap rows; pit_stops_measure or race_pitstop_summary are appropriate for pit-event analyses. | Use this view when you need the best lap per race or per driver (fastest lap) without additional grouping — WHY: this view contains all laps; selecting MIN(milliseconds) without partitioning/limiting can be error-prone. For pre-aggregated fastest-lap results prefer fastest_lap_per_race. | Use this view to represent final season-level rankings or points — WHY: season aggregates and ranks are not present; use driver_season_points, driver_season_rank, or constructor_season_points as appropriate.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need final race results (finishing position, total points for that race) — it has the race-driver grain and final result semantics whereas lap_times has transient per-lap positions that vary within a race. | use pit_stops_measure or race_pitstop_summary instead when you need pit stop events or summaries — they have event/aggregate pit stop rows, whereas lap_times only captures lap-level timing and may not represent pit stop details reliably. | use fastest_lap_per_race instead when you need each race's fastest lap or fastest-lap holder — it is pre-aggregated at the race (or driver-race) level for that purpose; lap_times requires careful grouping/partitioning to derive the same. | use driver_lap_aggregates when you want aggregated metrics across laps for a driver (e.g., average lap time, lap count) — driver_lap_aggregates is already aggregated at the driver/race or driver-season grain, avoiding grouping mistakes that are easy when reusing the raw lap rows. | use qualifying_grid when your question concerns starting grid positions — qualifying_grid captures starting position semantics, whereas lap_times.position is an in-race, per-lap position that should not be used as starting grid without verification.

views.description: Clean projection of lap_times with numeric milliseconds and original time string. Useful for per-lap analyses, pace calculations, and joining to driver/race dimensions. | Use for: Per-lap fastest times, average lap time per driver/race; Compare lap times across drivers or laps

views.name: pit_stops_measure
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  stop,
  lap,
  time,
  duration,
  milliseconds
FROM pit_stops

params.when_to_use: Find the exact pit stop records for a specific race and driver (and specific stop number). Example: “Show all pit stops for race_id = 5 and driver_id = 23.” | List pit stop details (lap, time, duration, milliseconds) at their lowest recorded grain: one row per race_id, driver_id, stop. | Join to other dimension tables when you need the raw pit stop rows before performing any aggregation (e.g., to compute custom aggregates like average pit duration per driver using explicit GROUP BY on these rows). | Audit or validate source pit stop data because the view surfaces the raw columns directly from the pit_stops table without additional filtering or aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to ask questions aggregated by race or driver without explicitly aggregating here — using it as if it were aggregated (for example, 'pit stops per race') will double-count rows unless you GROUP BY the correct keys. WHY: the grain is per (race_id, driver_id, stop), not per race. | Do not use it to get a summary/cohort-level metric (e.g., average pit time per driver-season) expecting the view to collapse stop rows — WHY: it returns raw stops and will return multiple rows per driver if you forget to aggregate. | Do not assume it contains every driver or every race regardless of whether they had pit stops — WHY: this view only contains actual pit stop rows from pit_stops; drivers/races without pit stops are absent (inner/cohort filter). | Do not reuse it when you need a computed or ranked value (for example, fastest pit stop per race) unless you derive that aggregation yourself — WHY: no aggregation/filters are applied and it does not de-duplicate or rank stop rows. | Avoid using it as a substitute for lap-level timing tables when you need lap-by-lap telemetry or multiple lap events per driver — WHY: this view reports only pit stop laps, not every lap from lap_times_measure.
params.comparison: use race_pitstop_summary instead when you want pre-aggregated pit stop metrics per race (e.g., total pit stops, average duration per race) — it has aggregated summaries while pit_stops_measure is raw rows. | use lap_times_measure instead when you need full lap telemetry or to analyze lap sequences including non-pit laps — lap_times_measure has one row per lap event while pit_stops_measure only has pit-stop rows. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor when you need final race results or to join pit stop info to finishing positions in a single, denormalized result — those siblings integrate results data while pit_stops_measure contains only pit stop columns. | use driver_season_points or constructor_season_points when your question is about season-level points/standings — those are aggregated at the season/cohort level while pit_stops_measure is per stop. | use fastest_lap_per_race when you need one-row-per-race metrics like the fastest lap — that view is already reduced to the desired aggregation/selection while pit_stops_measure is not.

views.description: Projection of pit_stops events preserving per-stop grain and numeric milliseconds. Use for pit strategy and stop-duration analyses. | Use for: Count pit stops per driver/race; Average pit stop duration by team/year

views.name: results_fact
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  result_id,
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  constructor_id,
  number,
  grid,
  position,
  position_text,
  position_order,
  points,
  laps,
  time,
  milliseconds,
  fastest_lap,
  rank,
  fastest_lap_time,
  fastest_lap_speed,
  status_id
FROM results

params.when_to_use: When you need one row per race result (result-level facts) identified by result_id — e.g., list all results for a race or a driver with their recorded finishing position, points, laps, times and status. | When you need to join result-level attributes to dimension tables (race, driver, constructor) using result_id → race_id/driver_id/constructor_id while preserving the original result-level grain. | When you need raw, unaggregated result metrics (grid, position, position_text, position_order, points, laps, time, milliseconds, fastest_lap, rank, fastest_lap_time, fastest_lap_speed, status_id) exactly as stored in the results table. | When you want to compute aggregates (SUM points, AVG laps, COUNT results) and you will explicitly GROUP BY result_id or by appropriate dimensions so that aggregation is applied after selecting at the result grain.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not reuse for driver-season or constructor-season aggregates (e.g., total season points) without first grouping by the season and driver/constructor — using this view directly will double-count or mis-aggregate because this view returns one row per result, not aggregated season totals. | Do not reuse as a lap-level table: it lacks lap-level detail (no lap_number, sector times, or per-lap identifiers). Using it for lap analyses will silently miss multiple laps per driver — it only contains fastest_lap and aggregate lap counts. | Do not reuse as a pit-stop or stint-level source: it has no pit stop identifiers or timestamps. Aggregating pit-related metrics from it will produce incorrect results or empty joins. | Do not reuse when you need canonical driver+constructor combined rows (e.g., driver-with-constructor attributes for display): prefer the results_with_driver_constructor sibling which ensures correct joins and adds dimension attributes — direct joins to dimension tables are possible but error-prone if you expect enriched attributes already present. | Do not reuse for ranking within a season or race without using the appropriate ranking view (driver_season_rank, constructor_season_rank); this view stores a 'rank' column but that may be a stored value with a particular calculation or context — reusing it without understanding its calculation can lead to inconsistent ranks. | Do not reuse for queries that assume absence of DNF/DNS filtering: position_text/position_order/status_id encode finishing status. If you silently exclude non-finishers without applying the same filters, cohort mismatches will occur (e.g., counting starters vs classified finishers). | Do not reuse this view as a de-duplicated source if your downstream logic assumes distinct drivers per race — if the results table can contain multiple result rows per driver (rare but possible in some sources), you must deduplicate explicitly; this view preserves whatever multiplicity exists.
params.comparison: use results_with_driver_constructor instead when you want result rows already enriched with driver and constructor attributes — it joins dimensions for display and reduces repeated join logic, while results_fact is purely the raw result table columns. | use driver_season_points (AGG) instead when you need precomputed per-driver season totals — it has the aggregated grain (driver + season) and avoids you needing to group the result-level rows yourself. | use constructor_season_points (AGG) instead when you need precomputed per-constructor season totals — it has the aggregated grain (constructor + season) and prevents mis-aggregation from summing result-level rows directly. | use fastest_lap_per_race (AGG) instead when you specifically need one fastest-lap row per race — results_fact contains fastest_lap/time/speed attributes but is still per-result and may include multiple drivers; the aggregate sibling returns the single fastest-lap record per race. | use lap_times_measure or pit_stops_measure when performing lap-by-lap or pit-stop analyses — those siblings have the appropriate fine-grained measures (lap_number, pit_stop_time, etc.) that results_fact does not. | use driver_lap_aggregates when you need per-driver aggregated lap metrics across races or sessions — results_fact only exposes aggregate fields like fastest_lap but not detailed lap distributions. | use driver_season_rank or constructor_season_rank when you need ranks computed over a season with a consistent ranking method — results_fact's rank column may be stored differently or context-specific and is not a replacement for a rank view computed with known rules.

views.description: Projection of race results preserving primary identifiers and key measures (positions, points, laps, milliseconds, fastest lap info). Use as the canonical results fact table for downstream analyses. | Use for: Podium finishers, points per race/driver/constructor; Join race results to lap_times or pit_stops for deeper analysis

views.name: qualifying_grid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructor_id = c.constructor_id

params.when_to_use: Fetch the qualifying session rows at the qualify_id (qualifier entry) grain — e.g., list all qualifying attempts/rows for a specific race or driver. It returns one row per qualify_id with driver and constructor attributes. | Display driver and constructor attributes alongside their qualifying times (q1, q2, q3) and qualifying position for a given qualifying entry or for all qualifying entries in a race. | Join qualifying details to other tables when you need the qualify_id as the atomic key (for example, to link a qualifying row to a telemetry table keyed by qualify_id). | Reporting or UI tables that show the qualifying lineup with driver names and constructor names without performing further aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view to answer questions at the race-level (e.g., “how many drivers qualified in race X?”) expecting a race-level single-row summary — the view is at qualify_id grain (one row per qualifying entry) and will return multiple rows per race. Using it as if it were aggregated will silently overcount rows. | Do not use it to compute season- or driver-level aggregates (totals, averages, ranks) without explicitly aggregating after selecting — the view contains raw rows and repeated driver/constructor attributes; aggregating without GROUP BY on qualify_id can produce incorrect results. | Do not use this view to get final race results or fastest laps — qualifying position is not the same as race result; using 'position' from this view to represent race finishing position is incorrect. | Do not use this view to filter by race-wide cohorts without ensuring you deduplicate qualifying entries when necessary — if a downstream query assumes one qualifying row per driver per race but the underlying 'qualifying' table can contain multiple attempts or session rows, you may get duplicate driver counts. | Do not reuse this view to obtain driver or constructor dimensional records independent of qualifying context — because it only contains drivers/constructors present in qualifying entries, it will omit drivers/constructors that did not take part in qualifying.
params.comparison: use race_basic instead when you need race-level attributes or a single row per race — qualifying_grid is per qualify_id and will return multiple rows per race while race_basic provides race-level normalized fields. | use driver_dim instead when you need a canonical driver dimension (complete driver attributes independent of qualifying participation) — qualifying_grid only includes drivers that appear in qualifying and duplicates driver attributes per qualifying row. | use constructor_dim instead when you need a canonical constructor dimension (complete constructor attributes independent of qualifying participation) — qualifying_grid only includes constructors tied to qualifying entries. | use results_fact instead when you need race results/finishing positions or race-level performance — results_fact contains post-race results, whereas qualifying_grid contains qualifying positions which are a different measure. | use driver_season_points or constructor_season_points when you need season-level aggregated points — qualifying_grid is not aggregated and will not provide season totals. | use fastest_lap_per_race or driver_lap_aggregates when you need lap/timing aggregates (fastest lap or lap-based aggregates) — qualifying_grid only exposes q1/q2/q3 qualifying times, not lap aggregates from races. | use results_with_driver_constructor when you want a joined fact of race results already combined with driver and constructor attributes — that sibling provides result-context rows (finish positions) whereas qualifying_grid provides qualifying-context rows.

views.description: Denormalized qualifying result with driver and constructor attributes. One row per qualify_id (driver in a race qualifying). Useful when analyzing grid performance with driver/constructor context. | Use for: Compare qualifying position to race grid/results; Driver/constructor qualifying performance

views.name: driver_season_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.driver_id,
  SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id

params.when_to_use: Give each driver's total championship points and number of races they scored in, per calendar year (season-level driver totals). | Compare drivers' season-long points within the same year (e.g., leaderboards, season summaries, season-over-season points for the same driver). | Join to driver_dim or constructor_dim when you need driver attributes alongside season totals for reporting or display (one row per driver per year). | Feed downstream ranking or award-calculation logic that expects one row per (year, driver_id) with aggregated points and distinct races count.
params.when_not_to_use: As a source of per-race or per-result detail — the view is aggregated to (year, driver_id) so it will silently collapse multiple race rows into one, losing per-race information. Using it to answer 'what happened in race X' will be wrong because race-level granularity is gone. | To compute points for a subset cohort defined by filters on result-level attributes not represented here (e.g., only sprint races, only races after a given date, or only results with a specific fastest_lap flag). The view pre-aggregates over all results in the year, so applying such filters after aggregation will be too late and produce incorrect counts/sums. | To count event participations that have a different notion of participation than DISTINCT race_id in results (for example if you need to count starts vs. entries vs. finishes). The view uses COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) which may under- or over-count depending on the desired participation definition. | As a source for fine-grained time-based trend analysis inside a season (e.g., points per round or per month). Year is the only temporal key — round-level/ race_date-level breakdowns are not available. | To calculate average points per race when some races for a driver are missing from results or when you need to exclude non-championship events. The aggregation assumes every relevant race appears in results and does not carry flags to exclude events. | To attribute points to constructors or to combine constructor and driver allocations correctly. Points are aggregated by driver_id only; reusing for constructor-level questions will misattribute shared or constructor-specific points.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need result-level detail (per race, per stint, or to apply filters before aggregation) — results_fact preserves the granular rows that this view aggregates away. | use driver_lap_aggregates when your question concerns per-driver lap-level metrics (average lap time, total laps) rather than season points — that view is aggregated at a different semantic level (laps) and includes lap-derived metrics. | use constructor_season_points when you need season totals attributed to constructors instead of drivers — it has the same aggregation intent (season totals) but groups by constructor_id so it attributes points correctly for constructor-level analyses. | use fastest_lap_per_race when the analysis depends on fastest-lap awards or fastest-lap points per race — that view captures lap-specific awards which driver_season_points does not. | use results_with_driver_constructor when you need to join driver and constructor attributes at the result level before aggregating (e.g., to compute points by driver for only races where they drove for a particular constructor) — it keeps the join context that may be required prior to aggregation.

views.description: Aggregate points per driver per year (season) by summing results.points across races. Useful for season totals, ranking drivers by season, or trend analysis. Grain: one row per year + driver. | Use for: Season standings by driver (points per year); Compare drivers' season totals or compute averages per race

views.name: constructor_season_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.constructor_id,
  SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
GROUP BY r.year, res.constructor_id

params.when_to_use: Compute total championship points scored by each constructor in a given calendar year (e.g., "What were each constructor's total points in 2018?"). The view's grain is one row per (year, constructor_id). | Produce season-level summaries that need the number of distinct races a constructor scored points in during a year (races_participated counts distinct race_id values present in results for that constructor/year). | Join to constructor_dim when you need constructor attributes (name, nationality) at the same season granularity. | Calculate season-level metrics that can be derived from total_points and races_participated (e.g., average points per race = total_points / races_participated), remembering the aggregation is already performed.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need per-race constructor points (grain race_id × constructor_id) — this view is aggregated by year, so you would silently lose the race-level detail. | Do not use when you need per-driver or per-team-member contributions within a constructor-season (e.g., points by individual drivers in that year) — the view aggregates across drivers via constructor_id and will mask driver-level differences. | Do not use to answer questions filtered by non-year time windows (e.g., specific race weekend, month, or range of races) because the grouping is by r.year; filtering by race_id or date after aggregation may be incorrect or impossible without re-aggregating at a lower grain. | Avoid using this view to count number of race entries (starts) or attempts: races_participated = COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) counts distinct races for which a constructor has results rows, not starts vs. DNFs vs. entries, so it can misrepresent 'starts' if results data omit certain statuses. | Do not use when you need to exclude or isolate specific result types (e.g., only sprint races, only feature races, only points-scoring positions) unless the underlying results table has been filtered prior to aggregation; this view includes all rows in results and sums res.points as-is. | Do not use for rank calculations that require tie-breaking or race-by-race point accumulation ordering — this view provides season totals only and loses race sequence information necessary for progressive ranking.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need the raw, unaggregated per-result rows (race_id × driver_id × constructor_id × position × points) — constructor_season_points is aggregated by year and hides per-result detail. | use driver_season_points instead when you need season totals at the driver granularity rather than constructor granularity — driver_season_points has the same aggregation concept (season totals) but a different grain (year, driver_id). | use results_with_driver_constructor when you need to filter or re-aggregate by driver and constructor together or to compute metrics that depend on both driver and constructor at race-level — constructor_season_points already sums across drivers and races. | use race_basic when you need race-level metadata (date, circuit, or race-specific filters) to restrict which races contribute to a season total before aggregating — constructor_season_points joins races only to access r.year, but does not preserve race-level attributes for downstream filtering. | use constructor_dim when you only need constructor attributes (name, nationality, etc.) without season aggregations — constructor_season_points pairs constructor_id with season metrics and is not a substitute for a dimension table.

views.description: Aggregate points per constructor per year by summing results.points across races. Grain: one row per year + constructor. Useful for constructor championship tallies and season comparisons. | Use for: Constructor championship points by season; Rank constructors by year

views.name: fastest_lap_per_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.race_id,
  lt.driver_id,
  lt.lap,
  MIN(lt.milliseconds) AS fastest_milliseconds
FROM lap_times lt
GROUP BY lt.race_id

params.when_to_use: Find the single fastest lap time (minimum milliseconds) recorded in each race (one row per race). | Compare races by their best lap time (e.g., rank races by their overall fastest lap). | Join to race-level attributes (race_basic) when you need the race's best-lap time as a race-level metric.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need the fastest lap for each driver within a race — this view returns one row per race only, so it will silently drop multiple drivers who may have identical or different fastest laps (wrong grain). | When you need the lap number or driver for the actual minimum time per race — because the query selects driver_id and lap but groups only by race_id, the returned driver_id and lap are not guaranteed to correspond to the MIN(milliseconds) and can be arbitrary (SQL non-determinism). Using them as the true owner/number of the fastest lap will be silently incorrect. | When you need all laps that tie for the fastest time in a race — this view collapses ties into a single aggregate fastest_milliseconds value and does not preserve multiple tied rows. | When you need per-driver aggregates (e.g., each driver's best lap within each race) or per-lap-level analysis — this view aggregates at race-level and will miscount or omit rows if reused at driver or lap grain. | When you need measures computed with additional filters/cohorts (e.g., only laps after pit stops, only laps in a specific stint) — this view aggregates all lap_times, so filtering after aggregation will produce incorrect results unless the original lap_times were filtered before aggregation. | When you need deterministic identification of the lap row that produced the minimum milliseconds — because driver_id and lap are not included in GROUP BY, they should not be relied on to identify the row that produced fastest_milliseconds.
params.comparison: use driver_lap_aggregates instead when you need per-driver-per-race best lap — it has per-driver aggregation (same source) but preserves the driver grain so you won't lose or misattribute driver-level minima. | use lap_times_measure instead when you need to apply filters or compute different aggregates at the lap-level (same source table lap_times) — it preserves lap-level rows and allows correct filtered aggregation. | use results_with_driver_constructor or results_fact when you need race-level metrics that should be joined with result/cohort information (same race grain) — those views explicitly join driver/constructor context and maintain clearer join keys, avoiding the ambiguous driver/lap attribution present here. | use qualifying_grid when you specifically need qualifying lap/grid information rather than aggregated lap_times (different but related grain) — qualifying_grid preserves the intended row-level mapping for qualifying context.

views.description: Per-race fastest lap by selecting the minimum milliseconds among lap_times. Outputs the driving row (race_id, driver_id, lap) with the fastest milliseconds. Use for identifying which driver set the fastest lap in a race (based on lap_times table). | Use for: Which driver set the fastest lap in each race?; Compare fastest lap milliseconds across races

views.name: driver_lap_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds,
  COUNT(*) AS laps_completed
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.when_to_use: Calculate per-race, per-driver lap-time summary statistics within a single race: e.g., “For each race and driver who drove laps in that race, what was their best lap time, their average lap time, and how many laps they completed?” | Join to race or driver dimensions when you need aggregated lap metrics at the (race_id, driver_id) grain to feed downstream aggregations (for example, compute season-level aggregates by further aggregating these rows by driver_id). | Reporting or ranking within a single race where each row represents one driver’s lap performance in that race (e.g., show best lap and mean lap for drivers in Race #X).
params.when_not_to_use: When you need lap-level detail (individual lap rows): this view is aggregated; using it will silently drop per-lap rows and prevent analysis that depends on lap-by-lap sequencing or lap_identifiers. | When you need session- or season-level aggregates without re-aggregating correctly: using these pre-aggregated metrics as if they were raw lap rows (for example, summing laps_completed across races to get season laps) is fine only if you aggregate correctly, but using averages (avg_milliseconds) from this view and averaging them again across races without weighting by laps_completed will produce wrong results (wrong aggregation/weighting). | When you need best/average across multiple races (season-best/season-average) without accounting for per-race aggregation: avg_milliseconds here is the per-driver-per-race mean; computing a season mean by simple average of these values treats each race equally rather than each lap equally, so it will be biased unless you weight by laps_completed. | When you need cohort filtering at the lap level (e.g., only count laps that satisfy some lap-level condition such as tyre compound or lap_number ranges): those filters must be applied to lap_times before aggregation; applying them to this view will be too late and can’t exclude specific laps. | When you need to detect duplicates or validate lap counts against official results that may include non-recorded laps or penalties: COUNT(*) is computed from lap_times and will reflect only rows present in lap_times; if lap_times is missing rows or includes warm-up laps, this view will silently reflect those issues. | When you need to join to qualifying or results datasets to compute e.g., gaps or finishing position–dependent lap metrics: this view contains no position, grid, or result info; joining without care can lead to incorrect cohorts (it does not restrict to drivers who were classified finishers).
params.comparison: use lap_times_measure instead when you need raw lap-level data — lap_times_measure exposes individual lap rows (same source) and allows filtering or conditional aggregates that this pre-aggregated view cannot support. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor when you need per-race finishing/cohort information (e.g., classified finishers, laps_completed according to official results) — those views include result/finish position context and are the authoritative source for race classification rather than COUNT(*) from lap_times. | use driver_season_points or driver_season_rank when your goal is season-level ranking/points — those siblings already aggregate across races to the season grain and implement correct season-level logic, whereas driver_lap_aggregates is per-race and would require careful re-aggregation and weighting to become season-level. | use fastest_lap_per_race when you only need each driver’s single fastest lap per race in a canonical way — fastest_lap_per_race may apply tie-breaking or join logic different from a simple MIN(milliseconds) and is intended specifically for fastest-lap semantics.

views.description: Aggregate lap statistics per race and driver: best lap (min milliseconds), avg milliseconds and lap count. Useful for comparing driver pace within a race. | Use for: Driver pace summaries per race; Identify drivers with consistent lap times or highest avg speed

views.name: driver_season_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dsp.year,
  dsp.driver_id,
  dsp.total_points,
  dsp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dsp.year ORDER BY dsp.total_points DESC) AS driver_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driver_id,
    SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
) dsp

params.when_to_use: Determine each driver's rank within a specific calendar year by total championship points (ties receive same rank) — when you need year-level driver standings. | Report per-driver season aggregates: total points and number of distinct races a driver participated in during a given year. | Produce leaderboards or season summaries that compare drivers only within the same year (partitioned by year). | Feed year-by-driver rows into downstream joins where the downstream logic expects a single row per (year, driver_id) representing season totals.
params.when_not_to_use: Don't reuse to get per-race or per-round rankings — the view is aggregated to year level (grain is [year, driver_id]) and loses race-level detail; using it for race-level questions will silently return identical values for all races in the year. | Don't use to compute rankings across multiple years or a custom multi-year cohort — the RANK() is PARTITION BY year, so it resets each year; reusing it for cross-year ranking yields incorrect ranks. | Don't use for queries that need points from a filtered subset of races (e.g., dropped rounds, only sprint races, or a date range) — the underlying aggregation SUM(res.points) includes all results joined to races; filtering after this view may miscount races_participated and total_points unless you re-aggregate correctly. | Don't reuse for calculations that require unique counting of participation at a different level (e.g., counting appearances per constructor-season or per round) — races_participated is COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) per year-driver; using it as-is for other cohorts misrepresents the participation metric. | Don't use when you need dense ranking or other tie-break logic — this view uses SQL RANK() (leaves gaps on ties); if your business rule expects DENSE_RANK() or to break ties by number of wins, this view will produce different ordering. | Don't use as a source of truth for driver or constructor attributes (names, teams) — it contains only driver_id and year, no descriptive or constructor fields; joining to a driver_dim or results_with_driver_constructor is required to attach attributes.
params.comparison: use driver_season_points instead when you need the same season-level point totals but want a view focused purely on points (no rank). — driver_season_points has the same year/driver grain and total_points but does not include a windowed rank, so it's safer to re-rank with custom partitioning (e.g., multi-year) or tie-breaks. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor instead when you need race-level detail, per-race points, or to apply filters to results before aggregation. — those sibling views preserve row-level result data so aggregations (sum/count) can be recomputed correctly for custom cohorts. | use constructor_season_rank when you need analogous ranking by constructor per year. — constructor_season_rank shares the RANK pattern but applies to constructors; prefer that sibling for constructor-level standings rather than repurposing the driver view. | use driver_dim when you need driver attributes (name, nationality, etc.) alongside these season metrics. — driver_dim provides descriptive columns absent from driver_season_rank, avoiding joins that might be incorrectly assumed to exist in this view. | use fastest_lap_per_race or driver_lap_aggregates when your question concerns lap-level performance across a season rather than season points and participation counts. — those are aggregated at lap or race-lap grain and should be used instead of this year-driver rank view.

views.description: Season ranking of drivers by total points. Uses a window rank over year partition to provide a driver_rank column; keep year, driver_id and total_points so downstream queries can filter rank <= K. Grain: one row per year + driver. | Use for: Top-k drivers by season; Filter drivers with rank <= K per year

views.name: constructor_season_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  csp.year,
  csp.constructor_id,
  csp.total_points,
  csp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY csp.year ORDER BY csp.total_points DESC) AS constructor_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.constructor_id,
    SUM(res.points) AS total_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.race_id) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.race_id = r.race_id
  GROUP BY r.year, res.constructor_id
) csp

params.when_to_use: What was each constructor's total championship points and how many distinct races they scored in, per calendar year (season) — i.e., rank constructors within the same year by their season points. | Produce a season-level leaderboard of constructors where each row represents one constructor in one year, showing total points, number of distinct races participated in (as inferred from results rows), and dense ranking by points order for that year. | Comparisons or visualizations at the season × constructor grain (year + constructor_id), where ordering by total season points is required (e.g., season standings table sorted by constructor_rank).
params.when_not_to_use: If you need the rank computed within any cohort other than calendar year (for example by season+country, by constructor+engine, or a sliding window across years) — this view partitions only by year so it will silently produce incorrect ranks for custom cohorts. | If you require ranking by a different metric (e.g., average points per race, weighted points, points excluding dropped rounds, or only championship points from specific race types) — this view orders by SUM(res.points) and will give wrong answers for other metrics. | If you need the exact number of races the constructor entered (including races with zero points) rather than COUNT(DISTINCT results.race_id) — this view counts distinct race_ids present in results, so races without any result rows for that constructor are not counted and will undercount participation. | If you need row-level (per race) information or per-driver aggregation (e.g., constructor contribution by driver) — this view is aggregated to season × constructor grain and cannot be safely reused for per-race or per-driver questions. | If you need ties handled with a different ranking method (e.g., DENSE_RANK, ROW_NUMBER, or custom tie-breakers) — this view uses RANK(), which leaves gaps after ties; reusing it where dense ranks are expected will misrepresent positions. | If you need to exclude or filter particular results (e.g., exclude disqualified results, only count points from certain race rounds, or apply a filter on results before aggregation) — this view aggregates all rows from results joined to races without filters, so silent inclusion of unwanted rows will produce incorrect totals and ranks. | If you require the rank relative to constructors after applying a post-aggregation filter (for example, 'top 5 constructors by points across all years') — because the RANK() is computed per year in the view, filtering afterwards across years will not recompute ranking over the filtered set and will yield meaningless constructor_rank values.
params.comparison: use constructor_season_points instead when you need the same season × constructor aggregates (total_points, races_participated) but want to compute a different ranking or custom tie-breakers — constructor_season_points provides the raw season totals without an embedded RANK(), so downstream ranking can use a different window definition. | use driver_season_rank when the question is about driver standings rather than constructors — driver_season_rank has the same RANK pattern but at the driver × year grain; do not reuse constructor_season_rank for driver-level ranking. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor when you need per-race or per-result level data (e.g., to count entries including zero-point finishes or to apply pre-aggregation filters) — those sibling views preserve row-level detail whereas constructor_season_rank is already aggregated, so reusing it prevents correct re-aggregation or filtering. | use race_basic or races (not listed as a sibling but implied) when you need season-level definitions, race dates or attributes to limit which races contribute to a season total — constructor_season_rank joins results to races only to obtain year; it does not expose race attributes to filter or adjust which races are counted.

views.description: Season ranking of constructors by total points. Produces constructor_rank for each year; useful for selecting top constructors or comparing relative positions across seasons. | Use for: Top-k constructors by season; Compare constructor ranks across years

views.name: race_pitstop_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id

params.when_to_use: Count and average of pit stops per driver in a specific race: e.g. 'How many pit stops did driver X take in race Y and what was their average pit stop duration (milliseconds)?' | Driver-by-driver pit stop summaries at the race level for reporting or joins keyed by race_id and driver_id. | Aggregations that should be computed at the (race_id, driver_id) grain and can tolerate AVG and COUNT semantics (AVG over all pit stop records for that driver in that race).
params.when_not_to_use: When you need pit-stop statistics at a different grain (race-level only): this view is per driver per race and will double-count drivers if you forget to further aggregate by race_id; use caution because summing pit_stop_count across drivers is valid for race totals but averaging avg_pit_milliseconds across drivers is NOT the same as computing a race-level average over all pit stop rows. | When you need session-, stint-, or lap-grain metrics: this view loses any information about lap_number, stint, tyre, or chronological order of stops and cannot produce per-stop or per-stint analyses. | When you need weighted or median duration instead of simple AVG: AVG(milliseconds) here is an unweighted arithmetic mean of the driver's pit stop durations for that race; it will misrepresent distributions with skew or varying stop counts if you intended a different summary (median, weighted by stint length, etc.). | When you need the identity or timestamps of individual pit stops: the view aggregates away individual pit stop rows. Any logic that needs to locate or filter specific stops (e.g., 'the first pit stop of driver X in race Y') cannot use this view. | When filtering on cohorts defined by pit stop attributes not present here (e.g., tyre compound used in stop, stop reason): since those columns are not carried, applying such filters after reusing this view will be impossible or silently incorrect. | When you need driver-season or constructor-level aggregates without explicit further aggregation: this view is at race+driver grain; reusing it as if it were driver-season or constructor-season will produce wrong cohorts unless you aggregate appropriately.
params.comparison: use pit_stops_measure instead when you need the original per-stop rows or additional stop-level attributes — pit_stops_measure retains individual pit stop records (same underlying table) whereas race_pitstop_summary has already aggregated them to race+driver. | use race_basic when you need race-level metadata or to join race-level attributes — race_basic is normalized for race attributes while race_pitstop_summary is an aggregate keyed by race_id and driver_id (different grain). | use driver_dim when you need driver attributes (name, nationality, etc.) alongside pit stop aggregates — driver_dim supplies driver descriptive fields; race_pitstop_summary only supplies driver_id keys and aggregated metrics. | use driver_season_points or constructor_season_points when your question is about season-long aggregates/points — those sibling AGG views are at the season scope, while race_pitstop_summary is scoped to an individual race x driver. | use results_fact or results_with_driver_constructor when you need finishing position, laps completed, or combined result+pit information — results_* views contain race outcome/context fields that race_pitstop_summary does not and operate at different analytical scopes.

views.description: Summary of pit stop activity per race and driver: total pit stops and average/median milliseconds. Useful for pit strategy comparisons. Note: SQLite doesn't have MEDIAN built-in; this exposes avg and count which are widely useful. | Use for: Identify drivers with most pit stops in a race; Compare average pit stop durations across drivers/teams

views.name: results_with_driver_constructor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  res.result_id,
  res.race_id,
  res.driver_id,
  d.driver_ref,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  res.constructor_id,
  c.constructor_ref,
  c.name AS name,
  res.number,
  res.grid,
  res.position,
  res.points,
  res.laps,
  res.milliseconds,
  res.fastest_lap
FROM results res
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON res.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON res.constructor_id = c.constructor_id

params.when_to_use: Get one row per result (result-level facts) for a race entry: e.g. show the driver, constructor and result metrics (grid, position, points, laps, milliseconds, fastest_lap) for each result_id. | Join additional per-result measures (e.g. pit_stops_measure, lap_times_measure filtered to a specific result_id) where you need driver and constructor descriptive fields alongside the result row. | Select driver or constructor attributes for a specific result_id or small set of result_ids (detail lookups) where the natural grain is result_id.
params.when_not_to_use: Aggregating across results expecting one row per driver or per race — this view is at the result_id grain, so aggregating without grouping by race/driver will double-count or split drivers who have multiple result rows (e.g. multiple entries across seasons or disqualifications). | Calculating season- or driver-level totals (points per season, total laps per driver) — using this view directly for season aggregates can produce incorrect cohorts because it does not include season or year; use a season-aggregated sibling instead. | Measuring per-lap or time-series metrics (laps as sequence) — the view only contains summary fields (laps, milliseconds, fastest_lap) per result; it is not the lap-level grain and will be silently wrong if used like lap_times_measure. | Filtering by driver attributes that are not present/complete — driver fields come from a LEFT JOIN on drivers; if drivers are missing, the view will still return result rows with NULL driver columns, which can silently include ghost results if you expect all results to have drivers. | Assuming constructor data is complete — constructor fields come from a LEFT JOIN on constructors; missing constructor rows yield NULLs rather than excluding results, possibly hiding missing-reference problems. | Using this view as the canonical 'results_fact' for aggregated fact-store semantics — there may be a dedicated results_fact sibling intended for fact-table semantics (deduplication, canonical keys, additional measures). This view is a straightforward join and may retain rows you would otherwise filter/clean in a facts table.
params.comparison: use results_fact instead when you need a canonical, cleaned fact table or when you plan to aggregate across results into season/team/driver totals — results_fact is the sibling expected for fact-level aggregations and may include additional cleaning, canonical keys or filters. | use lap_times_measure instead when you need lap-level detail (one row per lap) — results_with_driver_constructor is result-level and will undercount/aggregate lap-based metrics incorrectly if reused for lap queries. | use qualifying_grid instead when you need qualifying-session-specific positions or grids across sessions — qualifying_grid is built for session/qualifying grain while this view's grid is the grid value stored on the result row (may differ for qualifying analysis). | use driver_dim or constructor_dim when you only need driver or constructor attributes across all contexts — driver_dim/constructor_dim provide the canonical dimension rows; results_with_driver_constructor is a join that repeats those attributes per result_id and may include NULLs from LEFT JOINs. | use driver_season_points or constructor_season_points when you need season-aggregated standings — those siblings are pre-aggregated by season and driver/constructor and avoid the risk of double-counting that occurs if you aggregate results_with_driver_constructor yourself without grouping by season and other keys. | use fastest_lap_per_race when you need one fastest-lap-per-race metric — results_with_driver_constructor contains fastest_lap per result but will not deduplicate to a single fastest lap per race; using it directly to find race fastest laps can return multiple rows or the wrong row if you don't aggregate properly.

views.description: Denormalized race results joined with driver and constructor descriptive attributes. One row per result_id. Use when reporting results with human-readable names and codes. | Use for: Result listings with driver/constructor names; Filter results by driver name, constructor, or grid position
